name: MonarchDeviceFrame
title: DeviceFrame
wrapsNative: RoundedRectangle and Capsule shapes, aspectRatio(_:contentMode:), ScrollView for interactive content
summary: A phone or tablet outline around a preview, named as one image or, when interactive, as a group whose content can be used.
whenToUse: In a builder that shows how a link page, an email or a mobile layout will look on a device, next to the form that changes it.
whenNotToUse: Not as decoration around real app content, and not to show the app's own screens on a phone, where the frame would be smaller than the device it is on.
api: MonarchDeviceFrame.init(_ label: String, device: MonarchDeviceFrameDevice = .phone, screenSize: CGSize? = nil, statusBarTime: String? = nil, isInteractive: Bool = false, isFlat: Bool = false, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

options.name: label
options.description: What the frame shows, for example "Preview of your link page on a phone".

options.name: device
options.description: phone: rounded, with a camera island. tablet: a wider bezel and no island.

options.name: screenSize
options.description: The width the frame never exceeds and the height that sets the aspect ratio. 390 by 844 for a phone and 820 by 1180 for a tablet by default.

options.name: statusBarTime
options.description: Shows a decorative status bar with this time text.

options.name: isInteractive
options.description: Whether people can scroll and use the content.

options.name: isFlat
options.description: Leaves out the side buttons and the shadow, for dense layouts.

options.name: content
options.description: The screen content, laid out in the screen area and clipped to it.

states.name: presentational
states.description: The default. The content cannot be touched and the frame is read as one image.

states.name: interactive
states.description: The content is in a vertical ScrollView without indicators and its elements are reachable.

states.name: flat
states.description: No side buttons and no shadow.

appearance: The bezel, island and side buttons use the inverse background role and the screen the surface role, so the frame is dark in the light themes and light in the dark themes. The shadow is the extra-large elevation.
platformNotes: Dimensions follow the web: a 10-point bezel and 44-point corner for the phone, 14 and 28 for the tablet. The web sizes with separate width and height numbers; iOS takes one CGSize. The frame scales to the width it is given but its content is not scaled, as on the web. Low priority on a phone, where the frame is smaller than the device.
accessibility: The island, the status bar and the side buttons are hidden from VoiceOver.
A frame that is not interactive is one element with the image trait and label as its name; its content does not take touches.
An interactive frame is a container named by label, and the elements of its content stay reachable.
The bezel and the status bar are a drawing of a device and do not grow with the accessibility text sizes; the content inside follows Dynamic Type.
The side buttons follow the layout direction: the three volume buttons are on the leading edge.
edgeCases: Content taller than the screen is clipped unless isInteractive is true.
A screenSize with a side that is zero, negative or not finite is replaced by the device's size.
With unlimited width and height the frame takes the screen width and the matching height.
The top of the content sits under the island on a phone with no status bar; add top padding or pass statusBarTime.
